blocks.text: ODED, FATHER OF AZARIAH: “THE PROPHECY OF ODED THE PROPHET” (2 CHRONICLES 15:8) · TWO KINGDOMS
Oded. Known from two verses; whether he himself prophesied is a question of the text.
SCRIPTURE CALLS
Prophet
ERA
Two kingdoms 930–586 BC
IN THE DAYS OF
Asa
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW THE WORD CAME
Chronicles names him twice: as the father of Azariah, on whom the Spirit of God came, and in the words “the prophecy of Oded the prophet”.
THE CALL
How the word came
Chronicles names him twice: as the father of Azariah, on whom the Spirit of God came, and in the words “the prophecy of Oded the prophet”. 2 Chronicles 15:1 2 Chronicles 15:8
BEFORE THE KINGS
Before Asa
KING OF JUDAH
Asa
COMPANIONS AND OPPONENTS
Who stood with him, and against him
Azariah, his son
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
From the textScripture tells nothing more of Oded. 2 Chronicles 15:8
TRADITION SAYS
No tradition is recorded here.
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
Azariah's, and some words have dropped out
C. F. Keil (1872); W. E. Barnes (1899); Ellicott's commentary (c. 1878–1884)

W. E. Barnes: “Some words have fallen out of the text. Read, Even the prophecy which Azariah the son of Oded prophesied.” Keil sees no solution but a gloss or a gap; Ellicott suggests “Oded the prophet” may be a marginal gloss and notes there is “no variation in Heb. MSS.” The Latin Vulgate reads “the prophecy of Azarias the son of Oded the prophet” (Douay-Rheims); the Greek reads “the prophecy of Adad the prophet” (Brenton). 2 Chronicles 15:8 [109][60][13][103][7]
Azariah's, called by his father's name
Matthew Poole (1683–1685); Joseph Benson (1811–1818); John Gill (1748–1763)

Poole: “Of Azariah … who was also called by his father’s name Oded”, or “the son of” is understood; Gill: “rather Oded here is the same with the son of Oded”. 2 Chronicles 15:1 2 Chronicles 15:8 [82][4][34]
A prophecy of Oded the father, not recorded
“Some”, as reported by Poole and Gill; the Pulpit Commentary allows it
Azariah may have repeated an older prophecy of his father. The Pulpit Commentary says this is “open to possibility” but “not very likely”. 2 Chronicles 15:8 [82][34][90]
Oded is Iddo
Jerome, as reported by the Jewish Encyclopedia (1904)
Jerome “identifies Iddo also with the Oded of II Chron. xv. 8”; Keil calls this conjecture without “tenable foundation”. 2 Chronicles 15:8 [48][58]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 1
2 Chronicles 15
PASSAGES · 2
2 Chronicles 15:1 2 Chronicles 15:8
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
No words of Oded are recorded.
Chronicles does not say whether Oded was alive in Asa's day.
He is a different man from the Oded who met Israel's army at Samaria in the days of Ahaz (2 Chronicles 28:9).
